hook.text: Carbon pricing puts a cost on CO₂ emissions—making polluters pay for the climate damage their emissions cause.

buildup.text: Cap-and-trade sets a total emissions limit and lets companies trade allowances—the EU ETS is the largest example.

discovery.text: Carbon taxes set a direct price per ton—simpler to implement and more predictable for businesses planning ahead.

twist.text: Global carbon prices range from $1 to over $100/ton—most are too low to drive real change; economists suggest $50–150.

climax.text: Border carbon adjustments (EU CBAM) tax imports from nations without carbon pricing—preventing carbon leakage.

punchline.text: Price the pollution—and clean energy looks even cheaper.

quiz.question: What is a border carbon adjustment?
options: A tax on imports from countries without carbon pricing
